subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate use of appropriate language orally in specific situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use appropriate register in everyday communication (informal and formal) with diverse partners on grade-level topics/texts/issues
exemplar: • Identify formal situations. E.g. interactions between strangers on varied themes, announcements, standards for work, school and public offices and business settings. • Use appropriate language to participate in formal interactions. (No slang/jargon). • Identify informal conversations: E.g. casual or intimate relationship between friends and acquaintances, family and teammates, different situations in the classroom etc. • Use appropriate language to participate in conversations in the following situations: Greetings, requests, encouragements, partings etc. NB: Examples of informal language include; slang words, jargon, contracted forms and non-verbal communication.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate use of appropriate language orally in specific situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Ask questions that elicit elaboration and respond to others’ questions in conversation
exemplar: • Identify words that can help give elaborate responses to questions in conversation (e.g. why, how, for what reason). • Engage in conversation using these words to elicit elaboration E.g. Ama: Do you think girls should study courses in the male dominated areas? Aziz: Yes Ama: Why do you think so? NB: Includes gender, equity, equality, and inclusion issues. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate use of appropriate language orally in specific situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use appropriate language orally to describe experiences about oneself and others
exemplar: • Use o language: tense structures, variety of sentences, figurative expressions etc. o vocabulary: nouns, adjectives, adverbs, etc. to communicate about one’s experiences and those of others in specific situations e.g. the hospital, shopping in a market/supermarket, at a bus terminal/station, etc.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate use of appropriate language orally in specific situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Listen to and give accurate directions to familiar places
exemplar: • Use appropriate language (e.g. opposite, adjacent, a few metres away, ten minute-walk /drive, turn left/right) and landmarks (church, mosque, hospital, filling station, etc.) to give directions. • Direct different individuals using a range of these vocabularies and expressions appropriately to given locations.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate use of appropriate language orally in specific situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use techniques (voice modulation and eye contact) for effective oral communication
exemplar: • Converse using appropriate voice (pace, volume, tone, stress) e.g. word and sentence stress. E.g.: increase (noun) and increase (verb). • Maintain eye contact (look in the eyes/face of the person speaking, maintain appropriate posture and facial expression) in conversation. • Engage in conversation using voice modulation and maintaining eye contact. Monitor how your partner shows this in the conversation. Demonstrate appropriate non-interruptive verbal and non-verbal cues/responses to show attention. STRAND 1: ORAL LANGUAGE SUB-STRAND 2: LISTENING COMPREHENSION INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate the ability to listen to extended reading and identify key information © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Listen to level-appropriate text attentively and identify key information
exemplar: • Identify key points: o intent or purpose of the message (e.g. to inform, persuade, instruct); o the speaker’s enthusiasm and passion for the topic; o main idea (s) and supporting points. • Read out and cross check the information written.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate the ability to listen to extended reading and identify key information © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Listen to, discuss ideas and share opinions from a level-appropriate text
exemplar: • Listen to and write key points from texts/speeches/presentations. • Discuss key points identified and share opinions. STRAND 1: ORAL LANGUAGE SUB-STRAND 3: ENGLISH SOUNDS INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Articulate English speech sounds to develop confidence and skills in listening and speaking © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Produce pure vowel sounds (short vowels) in context
exemplar: • Identify and produce pure vowels e.g. /a/, /i/, /e/ in context. • Articulate pure vowels clearly in speech.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Articulate English speech sounds to develop confidence and skills in listening and speaking © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Produce pure vowel sounds (long vowels) in context
exemplar: • Identify and produce long vowels in context. E.g.: part, peel, bloom. • Distinguish between long and short vowels in context. • Listen to and produce sounds as used in connected speech.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Articulate English speech sounds to develop confidence and skills in listening and speaking © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Produce diphthongs in context (centring and closing)
exemplar: • Identify centring diphthongs e.g. /eǝ / /iǝ/ in context. • Identify closing diphthongs e.g. /au/, /ai/ in context. • Listen and distinguish between vowels and diphthongs in context. • Use vowels and diphthongs accurately in connected speech. STRAND 2: READING SUB-STRAND 1: COMPREHENSION INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate increasing confidence and enjoyment in independent reading © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Read and understand a range of texts using monitoring and mental visualisation strategies to interpret texts
exemplar: • Engage narrative texts and create mental pictures to aid understanding. • Read fluently to build confidence. • Engage in meaningful interaction with text and peers. • Monitor for understanding and self-correct where necessary. • Make connections with what is read to own experiences.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate increasing confidence and enjoyment in independent reading © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use prediction to assess and improve understanding of texts
exemplar: • Make predictions about the content of a text using: o prior knowledge; o typographical and visual features; o text features; o organisational patterns; o organisational structure. • Ask questions to form ideas. • Answer questions to elicit understanding (meaning). INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate increasing confidence and enjoyment in independent reading © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Generate and answer questions to increase understanding and independent reading of fiction texts
exemplar: • Read a text closely for implicit meaning. • Write questions to guide reading. • Look back at questions as you read and create a link with text. • Provide and interpret evidence to support understanding. • Answer questions accurately. • Use the answers to identify the main idea of the text.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate increasing confidence and enjoyment in independent reading © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use text structure to understand and read texts independently
exemplar: • Interact with a variety of texts. • Examine the topic sentences that give clues to a specific structure. • Identify how the structure (how the information is organised) of the text influences meaning. These may include: o description, o sequence, o problem and solution, o cause and effect and o compare and contrast. • Use a graphic organiser to make a chart of the text structure. • Write paragraphs that follow a specific text structure. • Read independently and identify how text structure helps with understanding other texts. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Read, comprehend and interpret texts © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Identify the main text features of a non-literary texts
exemplar: • Use samples of varied texts such as non-fiction – articles, formal letters (business letters, newsletters), etc. to identify text features (Print, Graphic, and Organisational): o Print Features: title, heading/sub-heading, bold Print, italics, caption, etc. o Graphic Features: Photograph with or without caption, Drawing, Diagram, Map, Graph, Chart, etc. o Organisational Features: Table of Content, Index, Glossary, etc. • Discuss how the text features aid in the comprehension of a text. E.g. o A title indicates the topic, subject matter or the main idea of an entire text. o Bold print signals important vocabulary and/or a phrase that is integral to understanding the content of a text.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Read, comprehend and interpret texts © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Interpret non-fiction texts pointing out attitudes, opinions, biases and facts
exemplar: • Write out essential questions. • Read the text. • Make connections between texts and personal experiences. • Research or make inferences and share opinions on biases and facts in texts. • Distinguish between facts and opinions in a range of non-fiction texts. Interpret the different attitudes exhibited by the choice of words in texts to support understanding. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Read, comprehend and interpret texts © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Interpret a non-literary text showing personal responses and supporting responses with textual evidences
exemplar: • Read a variety of texts discussing the main ideas. • Identify how a writer’s choice of words and intentions contribute to meaning. • Differentiate viewpoints with textual evidence. • Examine the impact of different viewpoints and how these contribute to meaning. STRAND 2: READING SUB-STRAND 2: SUMMARISING INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate an understanding in summarising
indicator_text: Use summarising to understand key ideas in a range of texts
exemplar: • Read a variety of passages and identify the main ideas. • Analyse and decide what is important. o Do not write the same words as the author. o Think and write in your own words. o Ask, “What is the whole write up about?” • Restate or map out the gist/main idea and key details. • Put up a defence for the choice/ answer. • Restate the main ideas in own words.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of textual evidence that supports a writing piece © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Determine and analyse central and supporting ideas of texts
exemplar: • Read a variety of texts for main ideas. • Identify the main idea/topic sentence in the paragraphs. • Identify supporting details and how these relate to main details in texts. • Summarise main ideas of texts in own words and peer edit it. STRAND 3: GRAMMAR USAGE SUB-STRAND 1: GRAMMAR INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply the knowledge of word classes and their functions in Communication. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Demonstrate command and application of nouns in speaking and texts
exemplar: • Identify noun types (common, proper, countable and uncountable, concrete) from passages. • Construct sentences using noun types. • Categorise plural noun forms (emphasis on irregular nouns) in passages e.g. mouse – mice, child – children, sheep – sheep, half – halves. • Use plural noun forms in paragraphs.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply the knowledge of word classes and their functions in Communication. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use types of pronouns accurately in speaking and texts
exemplar: • Explore the use of types of pronouns in narratives: o Personal Pronouns o Possessive Pronouns o Relative Pronouns o Reflexive Pronouns o Interrogative Pronouns o Demonstrative Pronouns • Use pronouns in contextual sentences. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply the knowledge of word classes and their functions in Communication. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Explore accurate use of adjectives in texts
exemplar: • Recognise the effective use of adjectives in paragraphs: o directly before nouns. E.g. Asiedu is an excellent singer. o with the verb “to be” to describe the subject of the sentence. E.g. Adzo was very tired. • Use adjectives with sense verbs (sight, taste, smell, touch, hearing) or verbs of appearance to modify the nouns, which come before the verb. E.g. The fish tasted awful. He seemed very upset.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply the knowledge of word classes and their functions in Communication. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Relate forms of verbs to everyday activities (Tense & Aspects) in context, role play, radio, TV, films and narratives Present Tense
exemplar: 1. Identify the use of verbs that show present tense and aspect in sentences o simple present tense – I wash a car. o present progressive – I am washing a car. o present perfect – I have washed the car. o present perfect progressive – I have been washing the car Past Tense 2. Identify the use of verbs that show past tense and aspect in sentences: o simple past tense – I washed the car. o past progressive – I was washing the car. o past perfect – I had washed the car. o past perfect progressive – I had been washing the car. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply the knowledge of word classes and their functions in Communication. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use adverbs to modify verbs accurately at the phrase and sentence level
exemplar: 3. Recognise the effective use of adverbs in paragraphs; o to give more information about the verb. E.g. She slowly entered the room. o to give more information about the adjective. E.g. The test was extremely difficult. 4. Explore using the first adverb to give more information about the second adverb in sentences. E.g. The cheetah runs incredibly quickly.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply the knowledge of word classes and their functions in Communication. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use conjunctions accurately to link ideas in everyday discourse
exemplar: • Explore sentences using coordinating conjunctions. E.g. for, and, nor, but, or, yet, and so. • Construct sentences using correlative conjunctions. E.g. either... or, neither... nor, and not only... but also. • Use subordinating conjunctions to link ideas. E.g. because, since, as, although, though, while, and whereas. • Use adverbs that function as conjunctions in sentences. E.g. until, after, or before. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply the knowledge of word classes and their functions in Communication. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Demonstrate command of the use of prepositions in daily discourse (TV, radio, social media, news, home, role play)
exemplar: • Use complex prepositions (more than one word) in constructing sentences. e.g. consist of, in front of, on behalf of, in view of, in spite of, due to, near to, because of, by means of, by dint of (hard work), etc. E.g.: o The tree is in front of the house. o The prefect spoke on behalf of the class. • Use complex prepositions to express: o place e.g. near/close to, in front of, out of, far from, by the side of, etc. o time e.g. in time of, about to, during the course of, at noon, for one week, etc. o reason e.g. due to, because of, on account of, as a result of, etc. o concession e.g. in spite of, apart from etc.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply the knowledge of word classes and their functions in Communication. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Identify and use determiners in speaking and texts
exemplar: • Identify determiners from texts. o Articles are the most popular types of determiners. E.g. definite article ‘the,’ indefinite ‘a,’ and ‘an.’ o Possessives provide context in a sentence by informing the reader what belongs to the subject, such as ‘our,’ ‘your,’ my,’ ‘their,’ ‘her,’ and ‘his’. E.g. Her car is over there. o Demonstratives (that, this, there, these, and those) identify an object based on its location. • Use determiners in sentences and paragraphs. E.g. That cat is very fat. An apple fell from the tree. Is your coffee on the counter? INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate command of structural and functional use of sentences
indicator_text: Identify and use subject and predicate in text
exemplar: • Distinguish elements of a sentence. • Use the knowledge of the composition of subject. • Know the composition of predicate of a sentence.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate command of structural and functional use of sentences. © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Demonstrate command and use of compound sentences
exemplar: • Construct independent clauses. E.g. Kofi arrived late. He missed the exam. • Join two or more independent clauses to form compound sentences using coordinating conjunctions (and, but, or, so, etc.) • Analyse compound sentences to identify the various independent clauses in them. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply knowledge of clauses in communication © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use dependent and independent clauses appropriately in speaking and writing
exemplar: • Recognise sentences as independent/dependent clauses in texts. E.g. We danced at the party all night long. • Construct sentences by combining dependent and independent clauses. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of the use of conditional tenses in communication © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use conditional sentences in communication to indicate a possible condition and its possible result
exemplar: • Construct simple sentences using the future time, e.g. We will go home tomorrow. • Construct complex sentences and analyse them to show the main clause and the subordinate clause(s). e.g. When we came, they were at a meeting. When we came – subordinate clause They were at a meeting – main clause • Use if- clauses appropriately in communication (to indicate varied possible conditions and their possible results). e.g. If it rains, we will get there late. • Analyse given conditional sentences (main clause and subordinate clauses). Note: In a Type 1 conditional sentence, the tense in the ‘if ’ clause is the simple present, and the tense in the main clause is the simple future. E.g. I will be happy if you come to my party. The ‘If clause’ is the condition while main clause is the result and the order of the clauses are not fixed. Conditional sentence Type 1 is used to communicate real situations. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate mastery of use of active and passive voice © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use passive sentences for a range of functions
exemplar: • Use the passive voice to: o describe processes. o talk/write about past actions (when who did we do not know them). o talk/write about past actions (when we know who did them). o write reports and other formal texts. • Construct sentences in the active voice (subject, verb and object). E.g. The class won the game. • Reconstruct active sentences into the passive voice. E.g. The game was won by the class.

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate mastery of use of active and passive voice © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Demonstrate use and command of reported speech
exemplar: • Compose sentences in the direct speech and change them to reported speech. • Report what people say in formal and informal situations. e.g. ‘She agreed she would meet me after school.’ ‘He regretted he was busy on Saturday and wouldn’t be able to come.’ ‘You admitted there wasn’t any homework.’ ‘He reported he had been walking along the road when the car hit the tree.’ • Compose news reports. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Show understanding and use of question tags in communication © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use question tags accurately
exemplar: • Listen to dialogues involving question tags. • Identify statements with question tags. e.g. ‘You’re not going to play football today, are you?’ ‘You like tea, don’t you?’ ‘She’s older than me, isn’t she?’ • Compose statements with question tags. STRAND 3: GRAMMAR SUB-STRAND 2: PUNCTUATION AND CAPITALISATION INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate use and mastery of capitalisation and punctuation in communication © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Identify and use punctuation marks (question, exclamation, full-stop, comma) in given texts
exemplar: • Identify and use punctuation marks (question, exclamation, stop, comma) in given texts. • Correct punctuation errors in paragraphs. STRAND 3: GRAMMAR SUB-STRAND 3: VOCABULARY INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate appropriate use of vocabulary in communication © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Apply vocabulary appropriately in specific contexts
exemplar: • Use appropriate vocabulary in specific contexts and situations. E.g.: 1. When asking for and giving advice Asking for advice: o I need some advice. I’ve no idea what to do. o What do you think I should do? o What would you recommend? o What would you do if you were me? o Do you think I should ...? Giving advice: possible suggestions o You could always … (go to the shop and ask for an exchange). o My advice would be to ... (take it back and ask for a refund). o What you need to do is ... (make a copy in case the original gets lost). o One thing you could do is ... (read your speech/presentation to a friend). 2. When agreeing and disagreeing Agreeing: o I tend to agree with you. o That’s a good idea. o I’m with you on that point. o I’ll go along with that. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS Disagreeing: o I see things differently. o I tend to disagree with that idea. o I agree up to a point. However, ... o You have a point there, but ... 3. when ordering food in a restaurant 4. when speaking at a friend’s birthday party 5. when in conversation with peers, adults etc. Communication

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of use of aesthetic language to enrich communication © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Explore the use of proverbs to enrich communication Personal
exemplar: • Identify and examine proverbs in context to figure out their meanings. Creativity • Find Ghanaian proverbs to match the English ones identified. Critical • Use proverbs to construct meaningful sentences. Cultural Digital Presentation STRAND 4: WRITING SUB-STRAND 1: PRODUCTION AND INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Develop, organise and express ideas coherently and cohesively in writing © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use cohesive devices (pronouns, punctuations and conjunctions) to link sentences
exemplar: • Consolidate basic understanding of compound sentences using conjunctions (connectives): nor, or, so, then, yet. • Write complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions: o time clauses: when, before, after, since, while, as, until o conditional clauses: if, unless o purpose clauses: in order to, so that o reason clauses: because, since, as o result clauses: so that o concessive clauses: although, though, while o place clauses: where, wherever o clauses of manner: as, like, the way. • Use pronouns to connect ideas in paragraphs: E.g. - subject pronouns (he, she, they, etc.) - object pronouns (me, him, them, etc.) - demonstrative pronouns (these, this, those, that) • Use appropriate punctuation (question, exclamation, full-stop, comma, quotation (speech) marks). NB. Use logical connectors, pronouns and the repetition of words, synonyms and antonyms to create a cohesive text (i.e. a text in which sentences and paragraphs are linked together to show meaning and beauty). INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Create different paragraphs on a given topic © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Organise information in a logical manner.
exemplar: • Write a paragraph beginning with topic (main) sentence and supporting sentences. • Organise sentences in a logical sequence to create a coherent paragraph that is appropriate for the text type (narrative, descriptive, instruction (directions), persuasive, explanation (notice), etc.). • Use logical connectors to link sentences in a paragraph: o ordering ideas: firstly, secondly, finally, etc. o addition: moreover, furthermore, in addition, etc. o similarity: similarly, likewise, in the same way, etc. o contrast: however, nevertheless, although, though, on the other hand, etc. o cause/effect: because, therefore, as a result, consequently, etc. o sequence in time: next, soon, after, then, later, suddenly, afterwards, etc. NB. Use logical connectors, pronouns and the repetition of words, synonyms and antonyms to create a cohesive text (i.e. a text in which sentences and paragraphs are linked together to show meaning and beauty). STRAND 4: WRITING SUB-STRAND 2: TEXT TYPES AND PURPOSES INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Develop, organise and express ideas coherently and cohesively in writing for a variety of purposes (description, narration, exposition/information and persuasion), audiences and contexts © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Write personal narratives using effective techniques incorporating descriptive details and logical event sequences.
exemplar: • Plan and record ideas detailing personal experiences or past events: o Use: - descriptive details (setting, experiences or series of events). - first-person point of view to convey feelings, experiences and thoughts. - appropriate grammatical structures. adjectives and adjective phrases for producing vivid descriptions adverbs and adverbials for describing how an action has been carried out connectors for showing sequence of events direct and indirect speech for variation and adding interest nouns and noun phrases (e.g., participants, objects) prepositions and prepositional phrases first-person pronouns • Edit/Proofread the writing for sense, meaning and effect (targeted audience reaction). • Publish writing using different media including ICT. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Develop, organise and express ideas coherently and cohesively in writing for a variety of purposes (description, narration, exposition/information and persuasion), audiences and contexts © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Use precise (technical) vocabulary, phrases and sensory language to convey a vivid mental picture of people and experiences
exemplar: • Describe people using precise words (e.g. He staggers, to say precisely how someone walks), phrases and sensory details (words that appeal to sight, sound, smell, taste, and touch). • Use appropriate grammatical structures: o adjectives and adjective phrases for producing vivid descriptions in paragraph o adverbs and adverbials for describing how an action has been carried out o connectors to show sequence of events and extend ideas o direct and indirect speech for variation and adding interest o nouns and noun phrases (e.g. participants, objects) o prepositions and prepositional phrase o first-person pronouns • Revise and edit the writing for sense or meaning, and effect (emotional reaction). • Proofread to self-correct or peer-correct. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Develop, organise and express ideas coherently and cohesively in writing for a variety of purposes (description, narration, exposition/information and persuasion), audiences and contexts © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Create advertisements to persuade a given audience to take decisions on products and services
exemplar: • Compose advertisement for the sale of products, services, events following appropriate format/style using process approach: e.g. o Title o body – information about the product or service including design and pictures, the buyer (target market/audience) and selling points (what is good about the product or service, why is the product or service better than others?) • Use: o the simple present for conveying timeless statements and facts o modals or imperative(command) for persuasive effect and hedging o mental verbs (e.g. I think, I believe) for conveying a viewpoint o verb phrases o rhetorical questions and repetition for persuasion • Edit/Proofread the writing for sense or meaning, and effect (emotional reaction). • Publish writing using different media including ICT INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Develop, organise and express ideas coherently and cohesively in writing for a variety of purposes (description, narration, exposition/information and persuasion), audiences and contexts © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Compose a paragraph to explain a process, social and natural phenomena (how to do or use something, how something works)
exemplar: • Write the steps taken to do or make something or how something works (e.g. rules of a game or sport, recipes, instructions on how to use a device, volcanic eruption, flooding) by: o writing the aim of the text o listing the materials needed o sequencing and/or describing items to be carried out or conditions to be observed o using appropriate text features (e.g., main headings, sub-headings, diagrams/illustrations, bullets/numbering) • Use: o adjectives and adjective phrases for describing materials and objects o connectors for showing sequence in steps o nouns and noun phrases (e.g., ingredients in recipes) o quantifiers for indicating amounts of ingredients and materials o simple present for indicating the timeless nature of procedures

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply writing skills to specific life situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Compose informal letters on varied topics using appropriate format
exemplar: • Identify features of informal letters (writer’s address, date, salutation, body, subscription, name). • Use the correct features of informal letters appropriately. • Write informal letters on a range of themes to friends and relatives. (E.g. of themes; school life, excursions, games, festivals etc.). • Correct errors of informal letters written by others. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply writing skills to specific life situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Compose formal writing (application, invitation, email, media texts) on given topics using appropriate format
exemplar: • Identify features of formal letters (writer’s address, recipient address, date, heading, salutation, body, subscription, signature, name, etc.). • Write formal letters to offices. (E.g. to the Headmaster/mistress, the Director of Education, the Assembly Man/woman, the SMC chairman/ chairperson, the PTA Chairman etc.). • Correct errors of formal letters written by others. • write notices to class or club members to provide updates on rules, schedules or programmes. • Create a variety of media texts for different purposes and audiences using appropriate forms, conventions, and techniques. • Reflect on and identify strengths, areas for improvement, and the strategies found most helpful in understanding and creating media texts. • Edit/Proofread the writing for sense or meaning, and effect (emotional reaction). • Publish writing using different media including ICT. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply writing skills to specific life situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
indicator_text: Take notes for academic and other purposes
exemplar: • Identify and record: o source information (title, author, date etc.) o headings to help you identify the key topics o key points, examples, names, new ideas o triggers to make your notes more memorable – such as mnemonics, colour or drawings. o further reading and ideas to follow up later. • Identify and select key ideas. • Organise ideas and make connections. • Plan and structure written assignments. • Write notes while listening to the teacher, reading a text, viewing a video recording or revising. • Edit/Proofread the writing for sense or meaning, and effect (emotional reaction). • Record/represent writing in a flow chart, illustrations and notes in other media including ICT. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: English Language
content_standard_text: Apply writing skills to specific life situations © NaC CA, Ministry of Education 2021
